errors.text: Misinterprets powder-based ink extrusion printing as high-pressure hot extrusion.
Replaces the required hydrogen de-binding and 1400 °C, 18-hour vacuum sintering treatment with an unsupported 800–1000 °C decomposition and 1100–1300 °C short-dwell extrusion schedule.
Treats oxygen solely as contamination to minimize, whereas the target process maintains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen for interstitial strengthening while preventing excessive alpha-HCP stabilization.
Omits the decisive water quench from 1500 °C that stabilizes the metastable single beta-BCC phase.
Does not reconstruct the sequential Ta-to-Nb-to-Hf/Ti/Zr hydride decomposition and associated in-situ alloying mechanism.
The claimed pressure range, sub-1% porosity, and yield strength above 1500 MPa at 1000 °C are not supported by the cited evidence.
